newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - stability, not prestige, key to EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - stability, not prestige, key to EMU entry.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer, stressing the importance of genuine convergence for EU economic and monetary union, said on Friday that countries must not be allowed to enter EMU on a political ticket.
Speaking in the northern German city of Munster, Tietmeyer said, "Only maturity in terms of stability policies, and not political prestige, can govern the selection of countries."
The Bundesbank has in the past expressed some nervousness about the fact that some countries, such as Italy, appear to have made participation in the starting phase of EMU an issue of national pride.

Tietmeyer, rejecting once again the idea that the central bank opposes EMU, said that, on the contrary, the Bundesbank's insistence on strict adherence to the Maastricht Treaty's criteria was aimed at ensuring the success of the project.
Such demands were also not simply a matter of building barriers to keep some countries out, he said.
"The argument that the call for strict meeting of the criteria should create a special "euro-fortress' within the community is not in line with the facts," he said.
"The euro core must of course remain open for all EU countries which want and are able to participate later."
